title: Commission Implementing Regulation amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072 as regards measures to prevent the entry into the Union territory, and the spread within it, of Aleurocanthus spiniferus, Agrilus planipennis, Chloridea virescens, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4, Hirschmanniella spp., Meloidogyne enterolobii, Raspberry leaf curl virus, Spodoptera ornithogalli, Spodoptera praefica, Strawberry leaf curl virus, Thaumatotibia leucotreta, Toumeyella parvicornis and Xanthomonas citri pv. viticola, as regards changes of protected zones in relation to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus and Erwinia amylovora, amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1941 and repealing Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1927
description:
Implementing Regulation 2019/2072 contains the list of Union quarantine pests, protected zone quarantine pests, and regulated non-quarantine pests (RNQPs). Furthermore, it lays down phytosanitary requirements for import and internal movement of plants, plant products and other objects that may pose a phytosanitary risk to the European Union.

This draft amendment of Implementing Regulation 2019/2072:

  • Delists Aleurocanthus spiniferus, Raspberry leaf curl virus, and Strawberry leaf curl virus as quarantine pests and repeals measures associated with these pests.
  • Lists the following species as quarantine pests and sets, where applicable, measures to avoid their entry and spread in the Union territory: Chloridea virescens, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4, Spodoptera ornithogalli, Spodoptera praefica, and Xanthomonas citri pv. viticola. 

Please note that Chloridea virescens and Spodoptera ornithogalli were already listed in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1941 as species that are not to be introduced into, moved within, held, multiplied or released in the Union territory.

  • Updates  requirements for import and internal movement, including addition/revision of the respective CN codes, for Agrilus planipennis, Hirschmanniella spp., Meloidogyne enterolobii, and Thaumatotibia leucotreta.
  • Lists Toumeyella parvicornis as regulated non-quarantine pest and sets measure to avoid its spread in the Union.
  • Introduces changes to the protected zones in relation to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus and Erwinia amylovora.

Clarifies and corrects some inconsistencies (e.g. change of scientific names).

title: Notice of Administration Order of Saudi Food and Drug Authority Ref. No. 16506 dated 25 October 2026 entitled “Temporary ban on importation of poultry meat, eggs and their products originating from Wielkopolskie in Poland”
description: Following the WOAH report dated 19 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Wielkopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Wielkopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

title: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives
description:
Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/SPS/N/TUR/126 on 20/06/2022. 

The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:

 

Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: 13 October 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonized with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.

 

•    The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.

•    E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.

•    For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.

•    E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.

•     E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.

•    The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabilizers) in some traditional fermented alcoholic beverages produced in the EU.

•    E 334 Tartaric acid (L(+)-), E 335 Sodium tartrates, E 336 Potassium tartrates, E 337 Sodium potassium tartrate, and E 354 Calcium tartrate have been removed from Group I and are now permitted only in specific categories with specified maximum usage levels. Their use in food enzymes and flavourings has also been restricted in Annex III.

•    In the “16. Desserts” food category, the scope of use for E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate has been expanded to include water-based gelatine-based desserts.

•    The scope of use for E 460 Cellulose powder and E 575 Glucono-delta-lactone has been expanded to permit their use in unripened soft spreadable cheese products within the “01.7.6 Cheese products” food category.

•    In the “04.1.1 Whole fresh fruits and vegetables” food category, the authorization for surface applications of E 471 mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids and E 903 carnauba wax for glazing purposes has been extended to include passion fruit, kiwi, and cassava. E 322 Lecithins and E 570 Fatty acids have been authorized under Annex III as carriers in preparations intended for polishing cassava.

•    E 960b Steviol glycosides produced by fermentation have been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This amendment includes E 960b in the existing “E 960a–960d: Steviol glycosides” group, allowing this sweetener to be used under the same conditions as other steviol glycosides.

•    In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the authorization for the use of E 466 sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (cellulose gum) has been revoked.

•    In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the use of E 301 sodium ascorbate has been authorized in microencapsulated vitamin A preparations used in infant and follow-on formulas.

•     In Annex III, Section 1, the scope of use for E 1202 polyvinylpyrrolidone has been expanded to permit its use as a carrier in colouring tablets intended for the decorative colouring of eggshells.

•     In the food category “16. Desserts; excluding products falling under categories 1, 3, and 4,” the use of E 200–202 sorbic acid—potassium sorbate is permitted only in unheated plant-based mousses.

•    The use of E 999 Quillaia extract is permitted in both solid and liquid food supplements (Categories 17.1 and 17.2). Additionally, provisions have been added to Annex III to allow its use as an emulsifier in flavourings.

•     E 412 guar gum has been banned in the “13.1.1 Infant formula” food category.

•    The following additions have been made to the list of food categories under Section D of Annex II:

          •    18.1 Processed foods not covered by Categories 18.2 and 18.3, excluding foods for infants and young children

          •   18.2 Meal-replacement foods intended for weight loss

          •   18.3 Foods specifically manufactured to reduce the gluten content of gluten-containing ingredients or to substitute gluten-containing ingredients

•    The following food categories listed under Annex II, SECTION D have been deleted. Authority over these categories lies with the Ministry of Health:

         •    13.1.4 Special medical-purpose dietary foods for infants and young children, as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Special Medical-Purpose Dietary Foods / Special formulas for infants

         •   13.1.4.1 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for newborns and special formulas for newborns

         •    3.1.4.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for infants and young children as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes

         •   13.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes (excluding those listed in category (13.1.4))

•    E 942 The sale of nitrous oxide to the end consumer is prohibited.

•   The phrase “Non-alcoholic wine-like products” has been removed from the name of the food category “14.2.2 Turkish Food Codex – Wine Regulation: Wine and Other Products.”

•    In the subcategories under the “08. Meat” category, the definition has been used instead of the word “sausage.” The term “sausage” (sausages) is used in EU countries to refer to meat products served in casings and is not limited to the narrower meaning used in Türkiye.

•    To prevent the uncontrolled use of sorbic acid and benzoates, which may be present due to carry over from ingredients in meatless çiğ köfte products, under the category “12.7 Salads and savoury/spiced spreads for sandwiches,” the following limits have been established for meatless çiğ köfte: E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate; E 210-113 Benzoic acid—benzoates at a maximum usage level of 200 mg/kg for each additive group. 

•     In the “14.1.1 Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Fruit Juices and Similar Products,” pickle brine has been excluded from the list of foods in the “Fruit Juices and Vegetable Juices” category where Group I food additives may be used. The use of E 210–213 (benzoic acid—benzoates) is permitted at a maximum level of 200 mg/l.

•    Additional restrictions have been introduced in Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Türkiye and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products.”

         •    In sucuk: water-holding agents in the E 400–469 range, E 235 natamycin, and E 553b talc are prohibited.

         •    In heat-treated sucuk, the following are prohibited: E 400–469, E 235 natamycin, E 243 ethyl laurol arginate, and E 553b talc.

         •    In pastırma, raw or cooked döner, poultry döner, and raw or cooked meatballs and poultry meatballs, E 400–469 are prohibited.

         •    All additives are prohibited in ground meat kavurma.

•    In Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Our Country and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products,” certain food additives are exempt from these restrictions.

         •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in çiğ köfte, meatless çiğ köfte, and mezze (such as haydari, Arnavut liver, fava beans, shakshuka, hummus, and similar dishes), E 267 (buffered vinegar) is exempt from this prohibition.

         •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in köme, pestil, bastık, walnut-stuffed sucuk, and similar products, as well as in baklava, E 330 citric acid is exempt from this prohibition.

 

This Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication with a transitional period as 31 December 2028. Products placed on the market before 31 December 2028 by food businesses operating before the publication date of the Regulation establishing this article, and foods containing these products, may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life.
titlePlain: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives
descriptionPlain: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/SPS/N/TUR/126 on 20/06/2022. The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: 13 October 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonized with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.•    The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.•    E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.•    For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.•    E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.•     E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.•    The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabilizers) in some traditional fermented alcoholic beverages produced in the EU.•    E 334 Tartaric acid (L(+)-), E 335 Sodium tartrates, E 336 Potassium tartrates, E 337 Sodium potassium tartrate, and E 354 Calcium tartrate have been removed from Group I and are now permitted only in specific categories with specified maximum usage levels. Their use in food enzymes and flavourings has also been restricted in Annex III.•    In the “16. Desserts” food category, the scope of use for E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate has been expanded to include water-based gelatine-based desserts.•    The scope of use for E 460 Cellulose powder and E 575 Glucono-delta-lactone has been expanded to permit their use in unripened soft spreadable cheese products within the “01.7.6 Cheese products” food category.•    In the “04.1.1 Whole fresh fruits and vegetables” food category, the authorization for surface applications of E 471 mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids and E 903 carnauba wax for glazing purposes has been extended to include passion fruit, kiwi, and cassava. E 322 Lecithins and E 570 Fatty acids have been authorized under Annex III as carriers in preparations intended for polishing cassava.•    E 960b Steviol glycosides produced by fermentation have been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This amendment includes E 960b in the existing “E 960a–960d: Steviol glycosides” group, allowing this sweetener to be used under the same conditions as other steviol glycosides.•    In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the authorization for the use of E 466 sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (cellulose gum) has been revoked.•    In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the use of E 301 sodium ascorbate has been authorized in microencapsulated vitamin A preparations used in infant and follow-on formulas.•     In Annex III, Section 1, the scope of use for E 1202 polyvinylpyrrolidone has been expanded to permit its use as a carrier in colouring tablets intended for the decorative colouring of eggshells.•     In the food category “16. Desserts; excluding products falling under categories 1, 3, and 4,” the use of E 200–202 sorbic acid—potassium sorbate is permitted only in unheated plant-based mousses.•    The use of E 999 Quillaia extract is permitted in both solid and liquid food supplements (Categories 17.1 and 17.2). Additionally, provisions have been added to Annex III to allow its use as an emulsifier in flavourings.•     E 412 guar gum has been banned in the “13.1.1 Infant formula” food category.•    The following additions have been made to the list of food categories under Section D of Annex II:          •    18.1 Processed foods not covered by Categories 18.2 and 18.3, excluding foods for infants and young children          •   18.2 Meal-replacement foods intended for weight loss          •   18.3 Foods specifically manufactured to reduce the gluten content of gluten-containing ingredients or to substitute gluten-containing ingredients•    The following food categories listed under Annex II, SECTION D have been deleted. Authority over these categories lies with the Ministry of Health:         •    13.1.4 Special medical-purpose dietary foods for infants and young children, as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Special Medical-Purpose Dietary Foods / Special formulas for infants         •   13.1.4.1 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for newborns and special formulas for newborns         •    3.1.4.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for infants and young children as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes         •   13.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes (excluding those listed in category (13.1.4))•    E 942 The sale of nitrous oxide to the end consumer is prohibited.•   The phrase “Non-alcoholic wine-like products” has been removed from the name of the food category “14.2.2 Turkish Food Codex – Wine Regulation: Wine and Other Products.”•    In the subcategories under the “08. Meat” category, the definition has been used instead of the word “sausage.” The term “sausage” (sausages) is used in EU countries to refer to meat products served in casings and is not limited to the narrower meaning used in Türkiye.•    To prevent the uncontrolled use of sorbic acid and benzoates, which may be present due to carry over from ingredients in meatless çiğ köfte products, under the category “12.7 Salads and savoury/spiced spreads for sandwiches,” the following limits have been established for meatless çiğ köfte: E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate; E 210-113 Benzoic acid—benzoates at a maximum usage level of 200 mg/kg for each additive group. •     In the “14.1.1 Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Fruit Juices and Similar Products,” pickle brine has been excluded from the list of foods in the “Fruit Juices and Vegetable Juices” category where Group I food additives may be used. The use of E 210–213 (benzoic acid—benzoates) is permitted at a maximum level of 200 mg/l.•    Additional restrictions have been introduced in Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Türkiye and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products.”         •    In sucuk: water-holding agents in the E 400–469 range, E 235 natamycin, and E 553b talc are prohibited.         •    In heat-treated sucuk, the following are prohibited: E 400–469, E 235 natamycin, E 243 ethyl laurol arginate, and E 553b talc.         •    In pastırma, raw or cooked döner, poultry döner, and raw or cooked meatballs and poultry meatballs, E 400–469 are prohibited.         •    All additives are prohibited in ground meat kavurma.•    In Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Our Country and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products,” certain food additives are exempt from these restrictions.         •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in çiğ köfte, meatless çiğ köfte, and mezze (such as haydari, Arnavut liver, fava beans, shakshuka, hummus, and similar dishes), E 267 (buffered vinegar) is exempt from this prohibition.         •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in köme, pestil, bastık, walnut-stuffed sucuk, and similar products, as well as in baklava, E 330 citric acid is exempt from this prohibition.This Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication with a transitional period as 31 December 2028. Products placed on the market before 31 December 2028 by food businesses operating before the publication date of the Regulation establishing this article, and foods containing these products, may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life.

title: Administrative Regulation No. 27/2026 Amendment to Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food"
description:
To further safeguard public health, enhance the efficiency of risk management, and promote harmonization between local regulations and international standards, the Macao Special Administrative Region Government has amended Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food". This amendment is based on the latest standards recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC), as well as those  established by major food-supplying countries and regions. This regulation has been scrutinized through risk assessment to ensure that it adequately protect public health in Macao, China.

The revised regulation establishes a total of 165 maximum limits (MLs) for specified heavy metal contaminants in specific food items, of which 92 MLs represent optimizations or new additions. 
A reasonable transition period of approximately 6 months will be granted following the official promulgation of the regulation. This will provide sufficient time for the food industry to adapt its importation and safety control processes, and for local testing laboratories to establish and validate the necessary analytical capabilities in accordance with the new requirements.

title: Notification of the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards Re: List of International Standards Complying with Mandatory Standards (No. 2)
description:
Whereas it is deemed appropriate to amend the Notification of the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards Re: List of International Standards Complying with Mandatory Standards, dated 27 November B.E. 2568 (2025), due to the recognition of additional international standards aligned with the requirements of the Ministerial Regulation Establishing Agricultural Commodity Standard for Peanut Kernels: Maximum Level for Aflatoxin as Mandatory Standard B.E. 2558 (2015);

The following provision shall be added as (e) under Clause 2 (1) of the Notification of the National Bureau of Agricultural Commodity and Food Standards Re: List of International Standards Complying with Mandatory Standards, dated 27 November B.E. 2568 (2025):
"(e) Food Safety System Certification Scheme (Food Safety System Certification: FSSC 22000) Version 6.0 issued by The Foundation for Food Safety System Certification".

Therefore, the international standards conforming to the Ministerial Regulation on the Establishment of Thai Agricultural Standard on Peanut Kernel: Maximum Level of Aflatoxin as mandatory standard B.E. 2558 (2015) are as follows:

1. The system standards or production system standards, namely:

(a) Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) complied with Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene or equivalent;

(b) Hazards Analysis and Critical Control Point System (HACCP) complied with Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene or equivalent;

(c) Food Safety Management System (FSMS) complied with ISO/IEC 22000;

(d) Global standard for Food Safety Issue 9. British Retail Consortium;

(e) Food Safety System Certification: FSSC 22000 version 6.0 issued by The Foundation for Food Safety System Certification.

2. Aflatoxin analytical standards established by a national organization or international organizations such as Codex Alimentarius (Codex), International Organization for Standardization (ISO), AOAC International (AOAC) or analytical methods published in manual or international journals or analytical methods with the validation results obtained through the acknowledge procedures.

This notification shall come into force on the date of its announcement (5 October 2026).

title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. …, issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: “Flavoured Milk” (No. 3)
description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk" (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.

The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection.

descriptionPlain: This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk" (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection

title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. …, issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: “Cow’s Milk” (No. 3)
description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk" (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.

a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.

b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.

c. Amend the name designations of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk"  to align with the raw materials used.

title:
Declaration of special measures: importation of certain products from certain third countries and territories (England) - The Trade in Animals and Related Products Regulations 2011 (SI 2011/1197);

Declaration of special measures: importation of certain products from certain third countries and territories (Scotland) - The Trade in Animals and Related Products (Scotland) Regulations 2012; 

Declaration of special measures: importation of certain products from certain third countries and territories (Wales) - The Trade in Animals and Related Products (Wales) Regulations 2011 (SI 2011/2379 (w. 252))
description:
These declarations of special measures are necessary to prevent the incursion of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) to the United Kingdom. 

The measures prohibit the import of hay and straw and certain animal by-products from animals susceptible to foot-and-mouth disease from any countries, or zones within countries, that are not recognised by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) as free of foot-and-mouth disease – either with or without vaccination. This is in line with the recommendations set down in Articles 8.8.28, 8.8.30, 8.8.32, 8.8.33 and 8.8.36-8.8.40 of the WOAH Terrestrial Code.

The prohibition does not apply to animal by-products if they are an intermediate product, a trade sample or research and diagnostic samples.
productsFreeText:
Hay and straw and certain animal by-products of animals susceptible to foot-and-mouth disease that fall within the relevant subsections of the following HS codes:

  • HS 04 – Dairy produce: milk, milk-based products and milk-derived products; 
  • HS 05 – Products of animal origin, not elsewhere specified or included: 0502 (pigs’, hogs’ or boars’ bristles and hair, and waste thereof); 0506 (bones and horn-cores, including powder and waste); 0507 (horns, antlers, hooves, nails, claws and related products, including powder and waste); and 0511 (other animal products not elsewhere specified or included, including relevant blood products); 
  • HS 12 – Oil seeds and oleaginous fruits; miscellaneous grains, seeds and fruit; industrial or medicinal plants; straw and fodder: 1213 (cereal straw and husks) and 1214 (hay and other forage products); 
  • HS 15 – Animal, vegetable or microbial fats and oils and their cleavage products; prepared edible fats; animal or vegetable waxes:1501 (pig fat); 1502 (fats of bovine animals, sheep or goats); 1506 (other animal fats and oils and their fractions); and 1518 (chemically modified animal fats and oils, and relevant inedible mixtures or preparations);
  • HS 23 – Residues and waste from the food industries; prepared animal fodder: 2309 (preparations of a kind used in animal feeding, including relevant dog chews and processed pet food); 
  • HS 30 – Pharmaceutical products: 3002 12 00 (antisera and other blood fractions) and 3002 90 30 (animal blood prepared for therapeutic, prophylactic or diagnostic uses); 
  • HS 31 – Fertilisers: 3101 (animal or vegetable fertilisers) and 3105 10 00 (goods of Chapter 31 in tablets or similar forms, or in packages of a gross weight not exceeding 10 kg), where comprising or containing relevant manure; 
  • HS 35 – Albuminoidal substances; modified starches; glues; enzymes: 3501 (casein, caseinates and other casein derivatives; casein glues) and 3502 (albumins, albuminates and other albumin derivatives);
  • HS 41 – Raw hides and skins (other than furskins) and leather: relevant products under 4101 (raw hides and skins of bovine or equine animals), 4102 (raw skins of sheep or lambs) and 4103 (other raw hides and skins); 
  • HS 51 – Wool, fine or coarse animal hair; horsehair yarn and woven fabric: 5101 (wool, not carded or combed), 5102 (fine or coarse animal hair, not carded or combed) and 5103 (waste of wool or of fine or coarse animal hair); and 
  • HS 97 – Works of art, collectors’ pieces and antiques: 9705 (collections and collectors’ pieces of zoological or anatomical interest), where comprising relevant game trophies or other preparations.

including the core - for a duration of at least 30 minutes, and the "HT" mark, indicating that the wood has been subjected to heat treatment, must be present on the wood or its packaging;orc) The woods surface of the wood must be completely cut to give it a square shape.No.Plants, plant products and other objectsOriginSpecial requirements190. Wood of Quercus  L., including that whichhas not kept its natural round surface, otherthan those specified below:- Chips, particles, sawdust, shavings, woodwaste, and scrap;- Casks, barrels, vats, and other coopers'products and parts thereof, of wood,including staves, for which there isdocumented evidence that the wood wasproduced by applying a heat treatment at aminimum of 176°C for 20 minutes;- Wood intended for the production ofveneer, keeping its natural round surface;- Packing cases, boxes, crates, drums and similar packings, whether or not used inthe transport of any kind of product, exceptdunnage which complies with the sameconditions stated in the PhytosanitaryCertificate as the wood dispatched, andwhich is produced from wood showing thesame host property and of the same qualityas the wood in the consignment. Pallets,box pallets, other load boards, palletcollars, and wood packaging materials inthe form of dunnage.Countries where Bretziella fagacearum isknown to occurThe wood:a) Has been squared so that the round surface is completely lost;orb) Is bark-free and the moisture content, expressed as a percentage of dry matter, is less than 20%;or c)  Is bark-free and has been disinfected by an approved hot-air or hot water treatment;It must be stated in the Phytosanitary Certificate; orç) It must be stated on the Phytosanitary Certificate that the wood has undergone a heat treatment, reaching a minimum temperature of 56 °C throughout its entire profile - including the core - for a duration of at least 30 minutes, and the "HT" mark, indicating that the wood has been subjected to heat treatment, must be present on the wood or its packaging;ord) If sawn, regardless of whether bark residues remain on it; it must be stated in the Phytosanitary Certificate that the wood has undergone kiln drying - expressed as a percentage of dry matter and achieved using an appropriate time/temperature profile - to reduce the moisture content to below 20%, and the wood or packaging must bear the marking “kiln-dried” or “K.D.”No.Plants, plant products and other objectsOriginSpecial requirements191. Chips, particles, sawdust, shavings, wood waste, and scrap obtained entirely or partially from Quercus L.Countries where Bretziella fagacearum is known to occurIt must be stated in the Phytosanitary Certificate that the wood:a) Has been subjected to a kiln-drying treatment to bring the moisture content below 20%, obtained with an appropriate time/temperature indicator, expressed as a percentage of dry matter;or b) Has been subjected to an approved fumigation treatment and information on the active ingredient, minimum wood temperature, dose (g/m3), and application (exposure) duration (hours);or c) Must state that a heat treatment at a minimum temperature of 56°C has been applied to the entire surface of the wood, including the core, for a duration of at least 30 minutes.In this context, it is important to ensure that the country-specific conditions and phytosanitary requirements indicated in the table are met for the importation of forest products derived from walnut and oak.

title: Notice of Administration Order of Saudi Food and Drug Authority Ref. No. 16506 dated 25 October 2026 entitled “Temporary ban on importation of poultry meat, eggs and their products originating from Wielkopolskie in Poland”
description: Following the WOAH report dated 19 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Wielkopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Wielkopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

description:
This Proposal seeks to amend the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code to align the following maximum residue limits (MRLs) for various agricultural and veterinary chemicals so that they are consistent with other national regulations relating to the safe and effective use of agricultural and veterinary chemicals:

Cyazofamid in specified plant commodities (Ginger, root).

descriptionPlain: This Proposal seeks to amend the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code to align the following maximum residue limits (MRLs) for various agricultural and veterinary chemicals so that they are consistent with other national regulations relating to the safe and effective use of agricultural and veterinary chemicals:Cyazofamid in specified plant commodities (Ginger, root).
productsFreeTextPlain: Foods in general
conformStandardRecommendation:
Certain proposed limits may differ from Codex limits.
The scientific methodology used by Australia to establish MRLs is consistent with international best practice and follows a rigorous scientific risk analysis including dietary exposure assessment to chemical residues from potentially treated foods. Countries set MRLs according to the good agricultural practice (GAP) or good veterinary practice (GVP) applicable to their region.  Agricultural and veterinary chemical use patterns differ between different production regions and countries as pests, diseases and environmental factors vary.  This means that Australian MRLs for agricultural and veterinary chemicals in food may differ from Codex standards. Australia’s residues assessment processes for agricultural chemicals are available at: https://apvma.gov.au/node/1037.  Australia’s residues assessment processes for veterinary chemicals are available at: https://apvma.gov.au/node/719.

conformStandardRecommendation:
Certain proposed limits may differ from Codex limits.
The scientific methodology used by Australia to establish MRLs is consistent with international best practice and follows a rigorous scientific risk analysis including dietary exposure assessment to chemical residues from potentially treated foods. Countries set MRLs according to the good agricultural practice (GAP) or good veterinary practice (GVP) applicable to their region.  Agricultural and veterinary chemical use patterns differ between different production regions and countries as pests, diseases and environmental factors vary.  This means that Australian MRLs for agricultural and veterinary chemicals in food may differ from Codex standards. Australia’s residues assessment processes for agricultural chemicals are available at: https://apvma.gov.au/node/1037.  Australia’s residues assessment processes for veterinary chemicals are available at: https://apvma.gov.au/node/719.

title: Draft Decision of the Collegium of the Eurasian Economic Commission on Amendments to Decision of the Customs Union Commission of 28 May 2010 No. 299
description:
The draft Decision amends Decision of the Customs Union Commission No. 299 of 28 May 2010 "On the Application of Sanitary Measures in the Customs Union".

The draft Decision supplements the said Decision with a new paragraph 2-2, establishing that where amendments are introduced to the Common Sanitary Requirements in respect of requirements for products included in the Common List of Products (Goods) Subject to Sanitary and Epidemiological Surveillance (Control) at the Customs Border and on the Customs Territory of the Eurasian Economic Union that are not the object of technical regulation under technical regulations of the Eurasian Economic Union, transitional periods (provisions) for the entry into force of such amendments shall be established where necessary.

The draft Decision also updates certain terminological references without changing the substance of the existing sanitary requirements.

title: The  Turkish Food  Codex  Communiqué on Distilled Alcoholic Beverages
description:
The  Turkish Food  Codex  Communiqué on Distiled Alcoholic Beverages was notified to the WTO through G/SPS/N/TUR/69/Rev.1 on 30 July 2025. 

The Communiqué  has been published in the Official Gazette dated 1 October 2026, numbered 33387. 

 

Provisional Article

(1) Food business operators operating before the publication date of this Communiqué shall comply with the provisions of this Communiqué by 1 July 2027.

(2) Food business operators operating before the publication date of this Communiqué shall comply with the provisions of the Communiqué repealed by Article 22 until they achieve compliance with the provisions of this Communiqué.

(3) Products placed on the market before the publication date of this Communiqué or for which official import controls have been completed before that date may remain on the market for eighteen months from the publication date of this Communiqué.

title: Proposals to Amend the New Zealand Food Notice: Maximum Residue Levels for Agricultural Compounds
description:
The document contains technical details on proposals to amend the current Notice issued under the Food Act 2014 that lists the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for agricultural compounds in New Zealand.

MPI proposes the following amendments to the Notice:

  1. The amendment of existing entries in Schedule 1, for the following compounds and commodities:
  • Acetochlor, to set a MRL at 0.04 mg/kg in green peas (without pods);
  • Clomazone, to set MRLs at 0.01(*) mg/kg in green peas (without pods), mammalian fat, mammalian meat, mammalian offal, milk, poultry fat, poultry meat, poultry offal, and eggs;
  • Cyantraniliprole, to set a MRL at 0.01(*) mg/kg in maize;
  • Flufenacet, to set MRLs at 0.05(*) mg/kg in maize, mammalian fat, mammalian meat, mammalian offal, poultry fat, poultry meat, poultry offal, and eggs, and 0.01(*) mg/kg in milk;
  • Fluxapyroxad, to set an MRL at 0.03 mg/kg in kiwifruit;
  • Isofetamid, to reduce the MRL for grapes from 0.08 mg/kg to 0.04 mg/kg; and 
  • Mesotrione, to set MRLs at 0.01(*) mg/kg in mammalian fat, mammalian meat, mammalian offal, poultry fat, poultry meat, poultry offal, eggs, and milk.

2. The addition of three new entries in Schedule 1, for the following compounds and commodities: 

  • Chlorine dioxide, to set MRLs at 0.1 mg/kg in cattle fat, 0.05 mg/kg for cattle meat, cattle liver, and cattle kidney, and 0.01(*) mg/kg in milk;
  • Sedaxane, to set a MRL at 0.1 mg/kg in potatoes; and
  • Spidoxamat, to set a MRL at 0.15 mg/kg in apples and kiwifruit, and 0.2 mg/kg in grapes.

3. The removal of one entry from Schedule 1, for the following compounds and commodities: 

  • Removal of the entry for propamocarb, as this compound is no longer authorised for use in New Zealand.

4. The addition of a new Schedule of compounds, Schedule 4, setting maximum residue levels for the following compounds and commodities: 

  • Azoxystrobin, to set a MRL at 5 mg/kg in blackcurrants.
  • Fenhexamid, to set MRLs at 1 mg/kg in cucumbers, and 2 mg/kg in eggplants, peppers (sweet), and tomatoes.
  • Flonicamid, to set MRLs at 0.2 mg/kg in cucumbers, and 0.4 mg/kg in eggplants, peppers (sweet), and tomatoes.
  • Fluopyram, to set a MRL at 5 mg/kg in caneberries.
  • Flupyradifurone, to set MRLs at 0.4 mg/kg in cucumbers, 0.9 mg/kg in peppers (sweet), and 1 mg/kg in tomatoes.
  • Fluxapyroxad, to set a MRL at 7 mg/kg in strawberries.
  • Lufenuron, to set MRLs at 0.8 mg/kg in peppers (sweet) and 0.4 mg/kg in tomatoes.
  • Methoxyfenozide, to set MRLs at 0.3 mg/kg in cucumbers, and 2 mg/kg in peppers (sweet) and tomatoes.
  • Penthiopyrad, to set a MRL at 3 mg/kg in strawberries.
  • Sulfoxaflor, to a MRL at 0.5 mg/kg in strawberries.
  • Spidoxamat, to set MRLs at 1 mg/kg in peppers (sweet) and 3 mg/kg in stone fruits.

Note: (*) indicates that the maximum residue level has been set at or about the limit of analytical quantification.

title: Department Circular no. 12 series of 2025 “Sequence of Compliance to Regulatory Limits for Implementing Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) of Pesticides and Maximum Level (ML) of Contaminants in Fresh and Minimally Processed Plant Food”
description: This regulation provides clarifications on the hierarchy of food safety standards that have already been established and adopted as technical regulations, serving as points of reference for government agencies, international trading partners and local stakeholders. The scope of this regulation does not cover any requirements for compliance with regulatory procedures, issuances, or laboratory analyses, or any other substantial compliance costs to the stakeholders nor the government agencies. Tailored to meet the specific needs of Food Business Operators (FBOs), it serves as a clear reference point for determining the applicable food safety standards. The regulation offers alternatives for the regulatory agencies and the FBOs in cases of unavailability of PNS and Codex standards to cater the needs of the stakeholders while ensuring the safety of the plant foods.

title: Draft of Circular promulgating the List of permitted plant protection products and the List of banned plant protection products in Vietnam
description:
Draft of Circular promulgating the List of permitted plant protection products and List of banned plant protection products in Vietnam in 2026. 

Circular including three parts: Draft of Circular, Annex 1 (List of permitted plant protection products in Vietnam) and Annex 2 (List of banned plant protection products in Vietnam).

This Circular adds 04 new plant protection active ingredients (Tiorantraniliprole, Fenmezoditiaz, Flufenoximacil and Tanin) to Annex 1 at the request of pesticide registration organizations or individuals in 2026. In addition, this Circular includes several new plant protection products containing existing active ingredients and mixtures that are already included in the list.

title: Amending, supplementing, and repealing a number of articles of Circular No. 48/2012/TT-BNNPTNT dated 26 September 2012 of the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development providing on the certification of aquaculture, crop, and livestock products produced in accordance with application of Good Agricultural Practices, as amended and supplemented by Circular No. 06/2018/TT-BNNPTNT
description:
The draft circular removes aquaculture products from the scope of Circular 48/2012/TT-BNNPTNT (as amended by Circular 06/2018/TT-BNNPTNT), which governs certification of products made in line with Good Agricultural Practices (VietGAP). After the change, the circular will cover livestock products only.

Key points:

Article 1. Amendment and supplementation of the title of the Circular

“Circular providing for the certification of livestock products produced in accordance with Good Agricultural Practices”.

Article 2. Repeal of phrases

1. Repeal the phrase “aquaculture,” in the legal basis for promulgation of the Circular.

2. Repeal the phrase “aquaculture,” in Article 1; in clauses 2, 3, and 5 of Article 2; and in Appendix II.

3. Repeal the Clause 1 of Article 4.

4. Repeal the phrase “aquaculture, aquatic animal health, and biology for the aquaculture sector;” in point a, clause 1, Article 6.

5. Repeal the phrase “products in the aquaculture sector;” in clause 1, Article 16.

6. Repeal the phrase “Appendix IXA,” in clause 1, Article 16.

7. Repeal the phrase “Directorate of Fisheries,” in point b, clause 4, Article 17.

8. Repeal the code “CGDG-VietGAP-TS 01/” in Appendix I.

9. Repeal the phrase “Aquaculture (TS)” and the phrase “The code of the first VietGAP certification body designated in 2012 by the Directorate of Fisheries is VietGAP-TS-12-01” in Appendix VII.

10. Repeal the Appendix IXA.

Article 3. Implementation provisions

This Circular takes effect from ______ 2026.

Article 4. Transitional provisions

1. Decisions on designating VietGAP certification bodies which issued by the Directorate of Fisheries (now the Department of Fisheries and Fisheries Surveillance) under Circular No. 48/2012/TT-BNNPTNT shall ceasee to be effective when this Circular takes effect.

         2. VietGAP certificated for aquaculture products which issued under Circular No. 48/2012/TT-BNNPTNT before this Circular takes effect may continue to be used until the expiry date stated on the VietGAP certificate.

        This Circular now covers only the livestock sector

        VietGAP certification bodies in aquaculture will operate in accordance with the regulations set forth in Decree No. 22/2026/ND-CP, issued by the Government on 16 January 2026.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine “On Approval of the Hygienic Requirements for Reducing Acrylamide Levels in Food”
description:
The draft Order provides for the approval of the Hygienic Requirements for Reducing Acrylamide Levels in Food.

The Requirements specify the food products to which mitigation measures to reduce the presence of acrylamide apply, establish the relevant mitigation measures for food business operators and set benchmark levels for acrylamide to verify the effectiveness of those measures.

The Requirements provide for differentiated mitigation measures for food business operators producing and placing the relevant food products on the market, including producers, retail operators and chain establishments. They also establish requirements for establishing programmes for own sampling and analysis, keeping records of the mitigation measures applied and the results of sampling and analysis, determining sampling frequency, and reviewing mitigation measures in light of the results obtained.

Food business operators producing and placing food products on the market shall apply appropriate mitigation measures to achieve levels of acrylamide as low as reasonably achievable and below the benchmark levels for acrylamide in food set out in Annex 1 to the Requirements.

The benchmark levels serve as indicators for verifying the effectiveness of the mitigation measures implemented by food business operators to ensure compliance with food hygiene requirements at all stages of production and distribution, within the framework of procedures based on the principles of the Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) system.

title: Draft of the Egyptian Standard ES 3495 for “Quick– frozen fish sticks (fish fingers), fish portions and fish fillets – breaded or in batter"
description:
Egyptian Standard ES 3495 for “Quick– frozen fish sticks (fish fingers), fish portions and fish fillets – breaded or in batter"  specifies the basic requirements and descriptive criteria for partially cooked or uncooked frozen fish products coated with batter and/or breadcrumbs, as well as the methods of inspection and testing thereof.

Producers and importers are kept informed of any amendments in the Egyptian Standard through the publication of administrative orders in the official gazette.

title: Add of prohibited host related with Radopholus similis
description:
The Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency (APQA), Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA) in the Republic of Korea, has added host plant of Radopholus similis, one of the prohibited quarantine pests of Korea, which is based on the result of Pest Risk Analysis (PRA).
 

The import of living and fresh underground parts of Leea amabilis from the regions or countries specified below will be prohibited, and this measure will be applied on consignment shipped on and after 13 October 2026.
 

- Products covered: Relevant parts of host plants (available in English, 2 pages) associated with Radopholus similis


- Regions or countries likely to be affected, to the extent relevant or practicable:
 North America: Canada, Mexico, United States of America
 Central America: All countries
 South America: All countries (except Chile)
 Africa: All countries
 Asia: Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, China (restricted areas: Guangzhou City · Maoming City and Shenzhen City in Guangdong, Fujian; and Hong Kong, China), India, Indonesia, Japan, Lebanese Republic, Malaysia, Oman, Pakistan, Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Chinese Taipei, Thailand, Yemen
 Europe: Belgium, Denmark, Estonia, France, Hungary, Italy, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden
 Oceania and the Pacific: Australia (except Tasmania), Cook Islands (New Zealand), Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam, Hawaiian Islands, Micronesia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue (New Zealand), Norfolk Island (Australia), Palau, Papua New Guinea, American Samoa, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga


Full information of prohibited host plants and countries (regions) related to Radopholus similis, can be found in the Attachment 1 (available in English)

title: Proposed Rule: Cut Flowers Regulations; Removal of Chrysanthemum White Rust-Related Provisions
description: APHIS is amending the regulations governing the importation of fresh cut flowers to remove requirements for the importation of specific types of cut flowers from the regulations, and to list them in the U.S. Department of Agriculture database called the Agricultural Commodity Import Requirements instead. We are also removing entirely any restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers of the genera Chrysanthemum, Leucanthemella, and Nipponanthemum from countries in which chrysanthemum white rust ( Puccinia horiana P. Henn., CWR) is known to exist. This rule will allow us to use a notice-based, streamlined approach to update the import requirements for cut flowers and remove CWR-specific restrictions on the importation of fresh cut flowers.

title: Notice of Decision To Deregulate Chrysanthemum White Rust and the Importation of Chrysanthemum spp. Cuttings, and In Vitro Plantlets, and Synonymous Taxa From Certain Countries Into the Continental United States [Docket No. APHIS–2021–0081]
description: APHIS is advising the public of our decision to deregulate Chrysanthemum White Rust and authorize the importation of Chrysanthemum spp. cuttings, in vitro plantlets, and synonymous taxa from certain countries into the continental United States as described in this notice. Based on the findings of the pest risk analyses, which we made available to the public for review and comment through a previous notice, we modified and updated the commodity import evaluation and pest list documents and determined that the importation of Chrysanthemum spp. cuttings, in vitro plantlets, and synonymous genera from certain countries does not pose a risk of introducing quarantine pests into the United States. (Federal Register, Vol. 91, No. 194, Thursday 8 October 2026, pp. 64325-64330)

title: Notice of Administration Order of Saudi Food and Drug Authority Ref. No. 14560 dated 8 October 2026 entitled “Temporary ban on importation of poultry meat, eggs and their products originating from Małopolskie in Poland”
description: Following the WOAH report dated 1 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Małopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Małopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

title: Emergency measures to mitigate the risk of introducing Meloidogyne enterolobii
description:
To prevent the introduction of Meloidogyne enterolobii into Japan, the MAFF required National Plant Protection Organizations (NPPO) of exporting regions/countries to certify that:

For Underground parts of the live plants being capable of planting for cultivation listed in the document attached:

  1. The plants are grown at a place of production or a production site (including a plant growth facility) where M. enterolobii has not been known to occur or was known to occur previously but has been eradicated; and
  2. The plants are inspected at the place of production or the production site during the growing season, and the growing medium and the underground parts of the plants are examined by an appropriate nematological test and found to be free from M. enterolobii.

Therefore, exporting regions/countries of the NPPO were required to include an additional declaration, for example, by stating that "Fulfills item 13 of the Annexed Table 2-2 of the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Plant Protection Act (MAF Ordinance No73/1950)".

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine "On Approval of Requirements for Extraction Solvents Used in the Production of Foodstuffs and Food Ingredients"
description:
The draft Order has been developed with the aim of establishing requirements for extraction solvents permitted for use in the production of foodstuffs and food ingredients.
The Requirements establish a list of extraction solvents permitted for use in the production of foodstuffs and food ingredients, the conditions of their use, maximum residue limits for extraction solvents in foodstuffs and food ingredients as well as general and specific purity criteria for such solvents.
These Requirements also apply to imported foodstuffs and food ingredients that have been produced using extraction solvents.
The draft Order also establishes that foodstuffs and food ingredients that complied with the requirements of the legislation on the safety and certain quality parameters of foodstuffs in force before the entry into force of this Order, but do not comply with the Requirements for Extraction Solvents Used in the Production of Foodstuffs and Food Ingredients approved by this Order, may be imported into the customs territory of Ukraine, produced and/or placed on the market for three years following the entry into force of this Order. Such foodstuffs may remain on the market until the expiry of their minimum durability date or “use by” date.

title: Proposed Maximum Residue Limit: Fludioxonil (PMRL2026-11)
description:
The objective of the notified document PMRL2026-11 is to consult on the listed maximum residue limits (MRLs) for fludioxonil that have been proposed by Health Canada’s Pesticides Regulatory Directorate (PRD). 

MRL (ppm)1 Raw Agricultural Commodity (RAC) and/or Processed Commodity 

20              Tropical and subtropical fruits; small fruits; inedible peel (crop subgroup 24A); sugar apples 

3.0            Bananas 

0.3            Tree nuts (crop group 14-11, except pecan nuts and pistachio nuts)2 

0.01          Pecan nuts 

 

1 ppm = parts per million 

2 The established MRL of 0.08 ppm for fludioxonil on pistachios, based on previously reviewed pistachio residue data, is not being revised. 

The commodities included in the listed crop groups/subgroups can be found on the Residue Chemistry Crop Groups webpage (https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/consumer-product-safety/pesticides-pest-management/public/protecting-your-health-environment/pesticides-food/residue-chemistry-crop-groups.html) in the Pesticides section of the Canada.ca website.

title: Fish products
description:
This addendum concerns the notification of the Ministerial Decree No. 209 /2026 (2 pages, in Arabic) that gives the producers and importers a six-month transitional period to abide by the Egyptian Standard ES 804 for "Canned Tuna and Bonito" (14 pages, in Arabic).

It should be noted that the Ministerial Decree No. 256/2016, which was formally notified in G/SPS/N/EGY/60/Add.2, dated 12 August 2016, mandated among others the earlier versions of this Egyptian Standard, and the draft of this Standard was formerly notified in G/SPS/N/EGY/60, dated 3 March 2015, G/SPS/N/EGY/60/Add.1, dated 13 May 2015 ,G/SPS/N/EGY/60/Add.3, dated 7 April 2026.

 

Worth mentioning is that this standard is technically identical with Codex Standard CXS 70-1981 "Canned Tuna and Bonito" adopted in 1981, revised in 1995, amended in 2011, 2013, 2016, 2018 and 2024.

Producers and importers are kept informed of any amendments in the Egyptian standards through the publication of administrative orders in the official gazette.

Date of adoption: 21/9/2026.

Date of entry into force: The day following the date of publication in the official gazette.

title: Department Circular No. 46, Series of 2026: Temporary Ban on the Importation of All Commodities Derived from Foot and Mouth Disease-Susceptible Animals, Their Products and By-products Originating from Algeria, Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Chad, Comoros, Côte d’Ivoire, Eritrea, Eswatini, Gambia, Guinea, Jordan, Kenya, Malaysia, Mali, Mozambique, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Sudan, Tanzania, Tunisia, Uganda, Viet Nam, and Zambia
description: The Circular institutes emergency measures for the importation of FMD-susceptible animals, their products and by-products originating from the specified countries. It bans the importation of FMD-susceptible animals, their products and by-products. It also sets conditions for commodities that remain allowed under the temporary restrictions, consistent with the Philippines’ import terms and conditions and regulatory requirements. The Circular further provides that non-compliant shipments shall be dealt with under DA Department Circular No. 14, Series of 2025, and that Veterinary Quarantine Officers/Inspectors shall stop and confiscate shipments of commodities classified as “NOT ALLOWED” at major ports of entry.

title: Department Circular No. 50, Series of 2026: Temporary Ban on the Importation of Live Cattle, Meat, and Meat Products, and Bovine Processed Animal Proteins Derived from Cattle Originating from the United Kingdom
description: The Circular institutes emergency measures concerning the importation of live cattle, skeletal meat and meat products, and bovine processed animal proteins originating from the United Kingdom. It temporarily bans the importation of these commodities; immediately suspends the processing, evaluation, and issuance of SPS import clearances for the commodities; and automatically revokes previously issued and approved SPS import clearances for shipments that have not arrived at Philippine ports. Shipments in transit, loaded, or accepted at the port of origin on or before the effectivity of the Circular may enter provided that live cattle were slaughtered, or products were manufactured, on or before 5 August 2026. Non-compliant shipments may be confiscated, re-exported, or destroyed at the importer/consignee’s expense. The Circular also requires more rigorous inspection of arrivals of meat and meat by-products derived from cattle, including live animals and bovine processed animal proteins.

title: Fumigation and Disinfection Procedures for the Importation of Plants, Plant Products, and Other Substances
description:
During the import of plants, plant products and other substances to Türkiye; The Phytosanitary Certificate - issued by the official plant protection service of the exporting country addressed to Türkiye and in accordance with the ISPM 12 (International Phytosanitary Measures-Phytosanitary Certificates) standard must accompany the product. Information regarding the treatment carried out in the exporting country must be clearly stated in the "Disinfestation and/or Disinfection Treatment" section of the Phytosanitary Certificates.

 

Where fumigation is carried out by the exporting country, whether at the request of the importing country (Türkiye) or otherwise, all treatments applied shall be fully specified in the relevant section(s) of the Phytosanitary Certificate (Disinfection and/or Disinfestation Treatment Section).  

 

Fumigation is an important pest control method for plants, plant products, and other materials, particularly in terms of controlling pests, reducing product losses, and meeting quarantine requirements. The Regulation on Plant Quarantine stipulates that fumigation must be carried out by the exporting country for certain products. However, even when fumigation is not required under the Regulation on Plant Quarantine, it is known that, in some cases, exporting countries fumigate consignments to mitigate the risk of products being exposed to contamination by harmful organisms during transportation. 

 

Because the plant protection products used for fumigation are toxic, they pose significant risks to living organisms, food safety, and the environment. In order to prevent such high risks and potential adverse consequences, the details of the fumigation treatment must be fully declared on the certificate for all consignments that have undergone fumigation, and the relevant fumigation documents must accompany the Phytosanitary Certificate.

 

Furthermore, according to ISPM-12, the specified treatments must be those that are acceptable to the importing country and that are carried out or initiated in the exporting country under the supervision or authority of the exporting country’s National Plant Protection Organization (NPPO) to meet the phytosanitary import requirements.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine “On Amendments to the Order of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 801 of 19 January 2026” (concerning the Requirements for Milk, Dairy Products and Spreadable Fats)
description:
The draft Order proposes to amend the Requirements for milk, dairy products and spreadable fats intended for human consumption, approved by Order of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture of Ukraine No. 801 "On Approval of Requirements for Milk, Dairy Products and Spreadable Fats" of 19 January 2026 (notified in document G/SPS/N/UKR/262), in particular with regard to clarifying:

the definition of the term "butter";

the permissible deviations from the declared fat content in spreadable fats by establishing the relevant tolerances in percentage points.

The draft Order is expected to enter into force on 1 January 2029, simultaneously with the entry into force of the Order No. 801 of 19 January 2026. 

The  draft Order is also notified under the TBT Agreement.

title: The Law on Fisheries
description: The Law on Fisheries promulgated on 28 June 2025 comprises 104 articles and divided into 15 chapters. This law defines the management, conservation, and development of efficient and sustainable fisheries, aiming to promote food security and the national economy, as well as ensuring the protection of the rights and benefits of fishers, community fisheries, aquaculture farmers, and fish and fishery products business owners. The law also focuses on food safety, facilitating trade and transit of fish and fisheries products. Additionally, it aims to contribute to socio-economic development, welfare promotion and public health while ensuring the sustainability of natural resources and fisheries-ecological system in Cambodia. This law reflects Cambodia's high commitment in harmonizing its food safety regulations to the International Standards.

title: Draft Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine “On Approval of the State Medical and Sanitary Standards for Maximum Permitted Levels of Radioactive Contamination of Food and Feed”
description:
The draft Order proposes to approve the State Medical and Sanitary Standards for Maximum Permitted Levels of Radioactive Contamination of Food and Feed following a nuclear or radiological emergency.
The draft Order establishes maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed, including contamination by strontium-90, iodine-131, caesium-134, caesium-137, plutonium-239 and americium-241 (Sr-90, I-131, Cs-134, Cs-137, Pu-239 and Am-241), and provides that the Standards shall apply for three months from the date of occurrence and/or receipt, in accordance with the procedure established by law, of notification of a nuclear or radiological emergency.
The Standards shall apply to food, beverages, including alcoholic beverages, and feed that have been or may be radioactively contaminated in the event of a nuclear or radiological emergency and that are produced and/or placed on the market in Ukraine, or imported (consigned) into the customs territory of Ukraine from the country of origin or consignment following such an emergency.
It is also established that the State Hygienic Standards “Permitted Levels of Radionuclide Content of ^137Cs and ^90Sr in Food and Drinking Water”, approved by Order of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine No. 256 of 3 May 2006, shall not apply where and to the extent that the maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination established by the Standards approved by this Order are applicable in accordance with the legislation.
The established maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed, including food and feed placed on the market, will contribute to protecting the population from the adverse effects of ionising radiation associated with the consumption of radioactively contaminated food and, indirectly, with the consumption by animals of radioactively contaminated feed resulting from a nuclear or radiological emergency.
